title: Make the folder chooser fast on network filesystems
description:
> **Stacked PR.** This builds on #204 (typed-path resolution) and on adapted versions of #196 and #201 (`3650a88`, `40d7518`), which sit on top of #204 on my branch. Until those land, the commit list and diff here include them too. **The new work is only the last three commits (`1a4b795`, `b38b817`, `ae27211`).** Once #204 merges, I'll rebase this so the diff shows just that.

## Summary

On NFS, opening the folder chooser on a 490-entry home directory made about **8,300 filesystem lookups**, against about 1,500 for the file chooser, and it was visibly slow. There were three causes, each fixed separately:

1. **A lookup per entry to find the folders.** Each entry got a `dir.exists()` call, which is a network round trip each. Now:
   - The tree asks `dir_ls()` for directories and symlinks only, and checks just those.
   - The flat listing (file chooser, save dialog, content pane) uses the type `file_info()` already returned, and resolves only symlinks.
   - The save dialog shares this code, so it gets the same fix.
2. **Every collapsed subfolder was listed** just to decide whether to draw its expand arrow. Now:
   - That happens *after* the response has gone out, so the tree shows immediately with every collapsed folder drawn as expandable.
   - The server then checks the collapsed folders on the event loop (`later`) in ~20 ms slices and tells the client which are empty (`shinyDirectories-empty`), so their arrows disappear without a click.
   - A newer response or the end of the session stops a check in progress.
   - The check reuses the root path already resolved for the response, so a slow `roots` function isn't called again.
3. **The whole tree was re-read on every click,** because the client sends its whole tree each time. Now:
   - Listings are kept per dialog while it stays open, so a click reads only the folder it touches.
   - They are dropped when the user could expect to see outside changes: reopening the dialog, refresh, an `updateFreq` tick, or creating a folder.
   - A request identical to the previous one is treated as a refresh, since the client only re-sends an unchanged input on refresh or an `updateFreq` tick.

## Results

Filesystem syscalls counted with `strace`. This doesn't depend on the NFS attribute cache, unlike wall time.

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Open folder chooser, home dir (490 entries) | 8,310 | 572 |
| Open folder chooser, fixture (480 entries) | 4,961 | 81 |
| File / save listing, home dir | 1,462 | 982 |
| Click in an open folder chooser: expand | 88–159 | 2–7 |
| Click in an open folder chooser: collapse | 153 | 1 |
| Click in an open folder chooser: highlight | 153–159 | 59 |

On the home directory in the example app, the tree draws in about 0.2 s, and the arrows on the 27 empty folders (out of 86) have cleared by about 1.5 s, with the dialog usable throughout.

The scripts and full tables are in `bench/`. Raw results are gitignored.

## Behaviour changes

- A collapsed folder with no subfolders shows an arrow for a moment, until the background check reaches it, or until it's opened if that comes first.
- While a folder chooser is open, folders added or removed **outside** it appear on refresh or reopen rather than on the next click. Folders created through the dialog appear straight away.

## Also in this PR

- **`later` added to Imports.** It's already a dependency of shiny, so nothing new gets installed.
- **Example app:** it now shows its source code below the app rather than beside it, so the sidebar gets the full width.
- **`dropRestricted()`:** the restriction filter that the flat listing and the tree both had inline is now one shared helper.

## Tests

- **`test-dir-listing.R`** (67 checks) checks the listings against an independent oracle (`list.files()` + `dir.exists()`). It covers:
  - symlinks to folders and to files, broken links, and a link loop
  - odd folder names
  - hidden folders and nested restrictions
  - unreadable folders
  - a folder deleted, or replaced by a file, between requests
  - that collapsed folders are never listed
- **`test-dir-cache.R`** (54 checks) drives a real `shinyDirChoose()` through `testServer()`, round-tripping each response through Shiny's JSON as the browser would. It checks:
  - that nothing is re-read, and that every answer matches a fresh read
  - that each invalidation point really shows outside changes
  - that two roots with same-named folders, or two folder choosers, don't share listings
  - restrictions and typed paths
  - for the background check: that it runs after the response, reports only truly empty folders with full paths, works in slices, stops when superseded or when the session ends, doesn't call `roots` again, and doesn't send the root's filesystem path to the browser
- **Mutation check:** making the cache never clear fails the 9 invalidation checks. Disabling the cache fails the 6 "no re-reading" checks.
- **`test-dir-tree-e2e.R`** (7 browser checks): arrows clear with no click, stay cleared after other clicks, and clear when a folder is opened.

The full suite passes locally (226 checks).

title: Offer recently used folders under "Recent" in the volume dropdown
description:
> **Stacked PR.** This builds on #204 (typed-path resolution) and on adapted versions of #196 and #201 (`3650a88`, `40d7518`), which sit on top of #204 on my branch. Until those land, the commit list and diff here include them too. **The new work is only the last commit, `aa6a301`.** Once #204 merges, I'll rebase this so the diff shows just that.

## Summary

When a selection or save is confirmed, the folder it was made in is remembered and listed under a **Recent** group in the volume dropdown, in every shinyFiles dialog on the page. Picking an entry jumps straight there, switching volume if needed.

- **Storage:** the list is kept in the browser's `localStorage`, not on the server. So it's per user and browser without the server needing to know who the user is (apps on Posit Connect often run as one shared account), and it survives reloads and app restarts.
- **Scope:** the storage key includes the page path, since many apps can share an origin, such as every app on one Connect server.
- **Safety:** entries are only root names and path segments, which is what the client already sends on every navigation. The server's usual containment checks still apply when an entry is chosen.
- **Filtering:** each dialog shows only the entries inside its own roots.
- **Configuration:** a new `recent` argument on `shinyFileChoose()`, `shinyDirChoose()` and `shinyFileSave()` sets how many to show. The default is 10 and `0` turns the feature off.
- **Ordering:** newest first, and confirming in a folder again moves it back to the top.
- **Failure mode:** if `localStorage` is unavailable, full or corrupt, the group doesn't appear and the dialog works as before.

## Notes for review

- This is **on by default**, so the dropdown changes for every existing app. Pass `recent = 0` to keep the old behaviour.
- All the logic is client-side in `inst/www/shinyFiles.js`. The R changes only pass the limit through.
- In the folder chooser, choosing a Recent entry sends an expanded chain of tree nodes down to the folder, the same shape the server builds for a typed path, so the destination renders.

## Tests

`tests/testthat/test-recent-e2e.R` has 20 browser checks (shinytest2). They cover:
- remembering on file select, folder select and save
- navigating from another button, and across volumes
- ordering, and moving a re-confirmed folder to the top
- hiding entries outside the dialog's roots
- `recent = 0`
- surviving a page reload
- a corrupt store

The full suite passes locally (118 checks).

title: Resolve typed paths against the configured roots
description:
## Summary

The path box behind the pencil button never resolved absolute paths. `setPathFromTextInput` tried to detect a volume in the typed text with:

```js
if (path.startsWith($(volume).val()))
```

but a volume option's `value` is its **name** (`"Home"`), not its filesystem path. That comparison never matches a real path, so typed text always fell through to the relative branch and was appended under whatever volume happened to be selected. Typing `/srv/data/project` with `Home` selected looked up `/home/user/srv/data/project` and reported *"Folder does not exist"* — even when `/srv/data/project` was inside a configured root.

It only appeared to work when the containing root was already selected, which is not discoverable from the UI.

The client can't fix this: it is only ever told root *names*, never the paths behind them. So the raw text now goes to the server in a `typed` field, and `resolveTypedPath()` matches it against the configured roots there.

**Resolution rules:** absolute input resolves against all roots, switching root when the path lives in a different one. When several roots contain the path the already-selected one wins (the listing is identical either way, so switching would only be jarring); otherwise the most specific root wins. Paths outside every root do not navigate.

The directory chooser renders a node only when its parent chain is flagged `expanded`, so `expandedTreeAlong()` builds that chain server-side too — the client can't, not knowing which root the text resolved to. This replaces the client-side tree walk, which also removes two accidental globals (`parent` and `tree`, assigned without `var`).

## Also included: a loading overlay

Related but separable — reviewable as its own commit (623ad84), happy to split it out if you'd prefer.

Listings on a networked filesystem can take seconds (expanding a directory with thousands of entries means a `stat` per child), and with no feedback that reads as a hang. An overlay now appears over the current listing — not replacing it, so a slow directory doesn't blank the dialog and cost the user their place.

It's raised on a 250ms delay, since most listings return well inside that and a spinner flashing on every click reads as a glitch rather than progress. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the animation is slowed rather than removed, as it's the only indication anything is happening.

Raised at every request site and cleared in every message handler. Three senders deliberately don't raise it: the final selection as the dialog closes, directory creation (which triggers its own refresh), and the initial listing — that one is pushed by the server when the dialog opens rather than requested by the client.

## Test plan

Adds a `testthat` suite (none existed). `R CMD check` is **Status: OK**; 44 tests / 87 assertions pass.

- [x] **Unit** (`test-typed-path.R`, 32 tests) — absolute input; root switching; selected-root vs longest-root precedence; `..` escapes; prefix-sibling roots (`/data` must not admit `/data2`); symlinks pointing out of a root; whitespace, trailing-slash and duplicate-separator normalization; `~`; non-character, multi-element and 10k-segment input; callable roots; roots configured with a trailing slash.
- [x] **Browser** (`test-typed-path-e2e.R`, 12 tests, `shinytest2`) — drives the real pencil dropdown, which is hidden until clicked and only submits on `keyup` with `keyCode 13`, so a resolver that's correct but unplumbed would pass the unit tests and fail these. Covers both choosers, `parseDirPath`/`parseFilePaths` round-trips, the expanded tree, escape handling, and that the observer survives an escape.
- [x] **Verified adversarial** — against the parent commit, 7 of 8 typed-path browser tests fail and 3 of 4 overlay tests fail. The ones that pass either way do so for understood reasons (an out-of-root path appended under the root didn't exist either, so it was already rejected — correct, but by accident).

Browser tests skip where no browser is available, so `R CMD check` stays clean without one.

## Notes for review

- **`fileGetter` already clamps** an escaping path back to its root rather than erroring; I left that behavior alone and added tests pinning it, so a typed path routed through the getter can't start serving out-of-root content.
- **A root of `/` means no containment** — every path on the machine is legitimately in-bounds. Pre-existing and arguably correct, but worth stating since it makes the escape cases look like leaks when testing with such a root.
- `RoxygenNote` is unchanged; `NAMESPACE` adds three `fs` imports. `DESCRIPTION` adds only test-time Suggests.

title: Trigger selection event
description:
Fix for #162

To test it use the following code:

```
library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)
library(shinyjs)
library(fs)

ui <- fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  headerPanel("Basic example"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      shinyFilesButton(id = "file",
                       label = "File select",
                       title = "Please select a file",
                       multiple = FALSE,
                       viewtype = "detail"),
      tags$hr(),
      shinySaveButton(id = "save",
                      label = "Save file",
                      title = "Save file as...",
                      filetype = list(text = "txt"),
                      viewtype = "icon"),
    ),
    mainPanel(
      h4(id = "text"),
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  volumes <- c(Home = fs::path_home())

  shinyFileChoose(input,
                  id = "file",
                  roots = volumes,
                  session = session)
  shinyFileSave(input,
                "save",
                roots = volumes,
                session = session)

  shinyjs::runjs(
    "$('#file').on('selection', function(event, path)
                                  {$('#text').text('Files button clicked');})"
  )
  shinyjs::runjs(
    "$('#save').on('selection', function(event, path)
                                  {$('#text').text('File save: ' + path.name);})"
  )
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: Check parent existence when attempting to navigate 'down' in directory selection
description:
This is a simple fix that should prevent infinite loops in the navigation behavior described in Issue #117 by checking that the parent directory exists before attempting to use it to find navigation targets.

When the last item in a directory (at any level) is selected and the user navigates 'down', shinyFiles attempts to 'bubble up' until a sibling can be found and used as a navigation target. Previously, this was allowed to create an infinite loop when navigating 'down' from the last item in the root. Essentially, shinyFiles was trying to navigate up the directory hierarchy infinitely.

title: fix for issue #112 by returning the epoch milliseconds from the server
description:
Previously, the server function `fileGetter` defined in file `filehoose.R` retrieves the files' creation and modification time and then convert them to date strings that don't include timezone information anymore thus causing issue #112 .

In this fix, I modified the `fileGetter` function so it returns the epoch milliseconds to the client side. This will also eliminate the burden to use `String.split` to parse the String on the client side because `new Date()` can directly take epoch milliseconds as the argument.

title: fixed issue #44 by using localStorage to cache the server file list
description: As my comment in #44 , the cached result can't be saved when the `fileChooseButton` is not rendered because currently the cache is bound to the DOM element. In this fix, localStorage is used to cache each file chooser's file list using its id as key.

title: Fix issue when launched from within a shiny modal
description:
This fixes an issue related to #101 where the filename text input could not be edited when launched from within a shiny modal. Here is a reproducible example:


```


library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)
ui <- fluidPage(

    # Application title
    titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

    # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins 
    flowLayout(
        actionButton("bt","nested"),
        shinyFiles::shinySaveButton("save_file2",
                                    "Save file2",
                                    "Save file2 as...",
                                    filetype = list(txt = "txt"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
    volumes <- c(Home = fs::path_home(), "R Installation" = R.home(), shinyFiles::getVolumes()())
    shinyFiles::shinyFileSave(input, "save_file", roots = volumes, session = session, restrictions = system.file(package = "base"))
    shinyFiles::shinyFileSave(input, "save_file2", roots = volumes, session = session, restrictions = system.file(package = "base"))
    
    observeEvent(input$bt,{
        d <- modalDialog(
            title="Save Document",
            size="l",
            actionButton("bt2","bt2")
        )
        showModal(d) 
    })    
    observeEvent(input$bt2,{
        d <- modalDialog(
            title="Save Document",
            size="l",
            shinyFiles::shinySaveButton("save_file",
                            "Save file",
                            "Save file as...",
                            filetype = list(txt = "txt"))
        )
        showModal(d) 
    })
}
# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

title: Force select on file double click
description: When selecting files, the 'dblclick' event now triggers a call to `elementSelector` with `forceSelect` set to `true`. This means, regardless of the status of the file that was double-clicked (selected or not) before the double-click, elementSelector will select the file.

title: use fs and tibble to address #87
description:
This PR address #87 and allow `shinyFiles` to work with files and directories with Chinese, Russian, etc. characters. It currently requires the GitHub version of `fs` due to [this issue](https://github.com/r-lib/fs/issues/133). 

There are also some up stream issues that, when addressed, will make this feature more useful. 

1. There seems to be a UTF-8 related issue in Shiny that prevents Chinese, etc., characters from being displayed correctly in `verbatimTextOutput`. However, the names are printed correctly in the Rstudio console if you try the updated shinyFiles example. See the screenshot below for an illustration.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2998956/44551641-9eadb400-a6dc-11e8-86c4-2795fd105ede.png)

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2135

2. There also seem to be some unresolved issues loading csv, rda, rds, etc. files that contain Chinese, etc. characters in R 3.5.1. See issue comment below. 

https://github.com/tidyverse/readr/issues/834#issuecomment-415308326

That said, based on my testing, the changes seem to be working well. Comments, suggestions, testing welcome

title: Rstudio icons
description:
This PR contains a few updates:

1. Add Rstudio icons. I requested and got permission to use several of Rstudio's file icons (e.g., .rda, .Rmd, etc.). This will help to limit confusion between what the user sees in the native / Rstudio file browser and in shinyFiles. Relevant statement added to README.md
2. It is common to place a text input and a button next to each other (see screenshot). Aligning the two inputs requires a `style` argument for the button.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2998956/43170673-18c936b8-8f5b-11e8-81ac-55316c255fcc.png)

3. On Windows I would see JS errors and no directory information when there are permission issue. Particularly for `dirchoose.R`. The updates in shinyFiles.js address all issues I encountered.
4. There were some typos in ui.R for the shiny example that I fixed. Also, I expanded the set of `roots` to show.
5. Added a function `find_home` that will always return C:\Users\me rather than C:\Users\me\OneDrive or whatever else Window decides to use

You can try out the branch using `devtools::install_github("vnijs/shinyFiles@rstudio-icons")`

title: Suppress warnings when obtaining file information
description: This PR address #57 by creating a utility function `.file.info()` that simply suppresses all warnings that could occur when running `file.info()` on certain versions of R on Windows.  I did not see any regressions to using this approach, and I have made sure that all previous calls to `file.info()` were replaced with the new `.file.info()` call.  If there was a more optimal way to do this I'm more than happy to revise.

title: Fix for #23 and #25
description:
My main goal was to address #25. By adding `actionButton` characteristics to `shinyFilesButton` the `observe` created by `shinyFileChoose` now isn't activated until the button is clicked. With this PR the example below will illustrate that the file browser is populated when `shinyFilesButton` is specified in the UI but also with renderUI. I expect it would be straight forward to apply a similar approach for selecting a folder and saving files.

I added `if (updateFreq > 0) invalidateLater(updateFreq, session)` to the `shinyFilesChoose` function so the user can set `updateFreq` to 0 when calling this function and deactivate `invalidateLater` if desired.

I commented-out all lines with `Shiny.unbindAll();` or `Shiny.bindAll();` in `shinyFiles.js`. Without this change, the approach described above does *not* work. Finally, I removed legacy code from `shinyFiles.js` as I expect this is no longer required.

cc @thercast

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)

# options(shiny.trace = TRUE)
```

title: change onAttach to onLoad so that the package doesn't have to be explicitly loaded; fixes #29
allow folder selection in shinyFiles
description:
I want to suggest this pull request as a way to resolve #8 

Folder selection is enabled by introducing the parameter `folder_select` in `shinyFilesButton that` allows the developer to enable/disable folder selection as a permissible choice in the file system navigator. This way mixed folder and file selection can be made permissible, e.g. with this example:

```
library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)

ui <- shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel('Multiple file and folder selection with shinyFiles'),
    sidebarPanel(
        tags$h4('Choose files and folders'),
        shinyFilesButton('file', 'File and folder select', 'Please select files and folders', TRUE, folder_select = TRUE)
    ),
    mainPanel(
        tags$h4('Selected files and folders'),
        verbatimTextOutput('filepaths')
    )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    shinyFileChoose(input, 'file', roots=c('R Installation'=R.home()), session=session, restrictions=system.file(package='base'))
    output$filepaths <- renderPrint({parseFilePaths(c('R Installation'=R.home()), input$file)})
})

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))
```

And although this should probably be implemented with an explicit flag, it even allows only folder selection capabilities if needed:

```
library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)

ui <- shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel('Single folder selection with shinyFiles'),
    sidebarPanel(
        tags$h4('Choose a folder'),
        shinyFilesButton('file', 'Folder select', 'Please select a folder', FALSE, folder_select = TRUE)
    ),
    mainPanel(
        tags$h4('Selected folder'),
        verbatimTextOutput('filepaths')
    )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    shinyFileChoose(input, 'file', roots=c('R Installation'=R.home()), session=session, filetype=c('NONEALLOWED'), restrictions=system.file(package='base'))
    output$filepaths <- renderPrint({parseFilePaths(c('R Installation'=R.home()), input$file)})
})

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))
```
